contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: cluster recovery resets the peer to a single-node cluster from local data; it is destructive for cluster membership state
contract_grounding.note: violates-declaration self-check (E5 improvement 2): the observed call site is OUTSIDE the quoted assertion's precondition domain. The constraint description scopes the operation to distributed deployments ('meant for permanently-lost quorum'); the sandbox is standalone (GET /cluster status='disabled', in-chain line 9-10), so the state promise (reset to single-node from local data) never came into play — the endpoint refused without any state mutation (state_cluster_recover_002 shows count intact and cluster plane 200 after repeated 500s). The surviving defect question is NOT on this state assertion's face: it is (a) the endpoint documents ONLY {200: ok} with no 5xx disposition documented, and (b) the 500-vs-400 error-class divergence from the server's own family convention for the same precondition. Those live on the behavioral/diagnostics faces (co-anchored sibling constraints qdrant_behavioral_cluster_recover_001 in candidates boundary_cluster_recover_002/003/004). Recorded honestly as violates=false on THIS constraint with domain explanation, not as vague partial.

source_grounding.note: The source DOES explicitly handle the standalone case — a deliberate coded check, not a panic/unwrap: the 500 is a deterministic refusal, so 'validation_absent' does not hold and no crash occurred. However, per the v3.4 tightened rule the deliberate-looking error cannot be marked by_design_in_source either: no comment/docstring/maintainer citation declares the 500 class intentional, and the same precondition is explicitly classified BadRequest(400) at three sibling sites — the divergence of error class within the server's own codebase is the recorded fact. Whether undocumented-500-for-standalone counts as a defect is the auditor's judgment.
